about.title: Paso Robles Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a collision on Rt 46E, US-101, or Creston Road takes someone's life, the days that follow are overwhelming. San Luis Obispo County traffic data shows Paso Robles sees traffic deaths each year, and behind every count is a family trying to make sense of what happened while also facing funeral costs and lost income. California law allows a spouse, domestic partner, or children to pursue a wrongful death claim, with other dependents or heirs sometimes eligible if none of those relatives survive. This is a separate civil matter from any police investigation or criminal charges, and it moves on its own timeline. Our team can review what happened, explain your options under California law, and help you understand what comes next, without any obligation or upfront fee.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Sooner Rather Than Later

items.title: Standing Rules Are Specific
items.desc: California law limits who can file a wrongful death claim, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children before other dependents or heirs. We can clarify where you fit and how to proceed.

items.title: The Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and that window shrinks significantly if a government entity is involved. Waiting too long can close the door on a claim entirely.

items.title: Losses Go Beyond Financial Support
items.desc: California allows families to seek compensation for loss of companionship and guidance, not just lost income or funeral costs. We can help make sure all recognized losses are considered.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Typically a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children have the first right to file. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may be eligible depending on the circumstances. We can review your family's situation and confirm who has standing.

items.question: How long do we have to file after a fatal crash in Paso Robles?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim. That deadline can be much shorter if the crash involved a government-owned road or vehicle, which is worth checking given how many Paso Robles collisions occur on corridors like US-101 and Rt 46E. Speaking with an attorney early helps avoid missing this window.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as a criminal case?
items.answer: No, a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action from any criminal charges that may result from the crash. The civil case focuses on compensating the family, while criminal proceedings, if any, are handled independently by prosecutors. Families can pursue a civil claim regardless of the criminal case's outcome.
